stoppedHere.reason: With the chain correct, the verifier's next static check surfaces a pre-existing, previously hidden condition: 18 destructive statements across 9 of the newly listed migrations have no entry in REVIEWED_DESTRUCTIVE_DISPOSITIONS. The stale list had been concealing them. Writing a disposition is a review act (each entry pins a statement AND asserts in prose why it cannot lose data), not the mechanical list update this lane was scoped to, so no disposition was invented, no migration was edited, and no assertion was weakened or removed.

stoppedHere.shape: Every one is an `if exists` idempotency drop or a constraint dropped and re-added in the same step — i.e. they look dispositionable — but that judgement belongs to whoever owns the security lineage, on the record, statement by statement.

replayNotReached: The static checks fail fast, so the three-database replay (build/catalog/RLS/grant/storage/remediation checks) never ran. It also could not have run here: scripts/rcap-schema-upgrade-lab.sh requires PostgreSQL 17 (the baseline grants MAINTAIN, which is 17+ syntax and cannot replay on 16); this container has only /usr/lib/postgresql/16 and no provisioned lab cluster. So this lane makes NO claim that the 16 added migrations apply cleanly, that the replay is deterministic, or that the upgrade reaches the accepted target schema.
